_comment: Fields below are graded BY HAND after collection. null = not yet filled.
_selfVerification: Did the harness review the running app in a browser (from the run log)? pass = reviewed and succeeded · partial = tried but failed · fail = no attempt. Note what it actually did.
selfVerificationNotes: fail/fail - no browser of any kind. All 27 shell commands are `ls`, `node -e` data/math scratch scripts, `pnpm init/add/build`, `node scripts/preprocess.mjs` and `git status`. No Playwright/Puppeteer, no headless Chrome, no vite preview, no screenshot, no DOM dump, no console capture. The closest thing to a runtime check is one `node -e` script that spins up a bare http.createServer over `dist/` on a random port and `fetch`es index.html, the JS and CSS assets and all five data files under a `/subpath/` prefix, asserting HTTP 200 on each ('ALL SUBPATH TESTS PASSED!'). That establishes relative asset paths resolve when served from a subpath - a real check, and more than most runs do - but it never executes the bundle, so it says nothing about whether the page renders or logs errors. It did run several genuine numeric self-checks against its own math before writing it (Earth-Sun distance at J2000 vs the expected 0.983-1.017 au; a computed asteroid-Earth distance vs a close-approaches.json nominal `dist`; hyperbolic/parabolic comet spot checks; Sentry and close-approach key join coverage; JSON parse timings) - but those all ran against Node scratch scripts, not the shipped code path, and none of them exercised the 3-iteration solver it actually shipped. consoleReview = fail, displayReview = fail. Not a budget problem: the run finished in 539 s.
_grade: Marks: pass | good | partial | poor | fail | na | null(ungraded). See RUBRIC.md. Score is computed by pnpm compile.
_tokenUsageNote: From the Cursor dashboard for this run (Cursor stores no token counts in its local DB). Input is fresh (non-cached) input only; 515,210 + 4,481,447 + 80,872 = 5,077,529, matching the dashboard total. Cache write is reported as 0, as on every other Cursor run.
costNote: Gemini 3.8 Flash list pricing (promotional rates in effect through 2026-12-31): $0.75/M input, $3.75/M output, $0.075/M cached input; no separate cache-write charge (implicit caching). 515,210 fresh input @ $0.75/M = $0.386 + 4,481,447 cache reads @ $0.075/M = $0.336 + 80,872 output @ $3.75/M = $0.303 -> $1.03. Cache reads are 88% of all tokens but only 33% of the cost. Token counts are UI-sourced (Cursor dashboard), not from a local log. Note list price doubles on 2027-01-01 ($1.50/$7.50/$0.15), which would make the same run ~$2.05.
